notes: Account profile: enterprise fintech, heavy regulatory needs (EU customers too). Will prefer Private deployment w/ VPC and optional on-prem later.
Primary technical contact: CTO Laura Mehta. Quote from discovery: "We need p99 chat under 180ms at peak with deterministic fallbacks."

Workload specifics: mix of multi-turn chat (stateful), question-answering over internal docs, reranking for search results, and embeddings indexing for similarity. Peak concurrency projected 350 concurrent sessions, average turn length 45 tokens, heavy tail to 4k token contexts.
Latency SLOs discussed: p50 < 50ms, p90 < 120ms, p99 < 180ms for short-context chat (<=2048). For long-context (>=8k) willing to accept p99 < 500ms but must be predictable.

Throughput goals: baseline target 10k tokens/sec sustained across reserved pool during market open; burst to 20k tokens/sec for 10-minute windows. Ops wants autoscaling/burst gating and cost predictability.

Reserved GPU planning: initial ask for 6 x A100-80GB to meet sustained throughput; Redwood recommended 8 reserved + 2 burst for headroom. Discussed pre-warming KV caches and dedicated KV-backed session routing.

Quantization strategy: SE proposed q4_k_m for prod-critical models (mix of int8-like and fp16 fallbacks). POC runs show q4_k_m reduces memory ~40% with 1.05x latency improvement on some kernels but increased perplexity on few vendor models. Need additional evals on fidelity-sensitive flows.

Context-length tuning: running dual-profile approach: short-profile (2k/4k context models, lowest latency) and long-profile (32k context, batched slower path). Smart routing rule to pick profile by request type and SLA.

Batching / KV cache policies: prefer small continuous batching (max batch 8) for chat to preserve latency; large batch windows for reranking jobs during off-peak; aggressive prefix KV caching for repeat prompts (TTL 4h) - also testing sticky-session routing to maintain GPU locality.

SLA negotiation points: uptime 99.9% for Dedicated control plane, latency credits for p99 misses, escalation path to Redwood SRE with 30min response for Sev1. Legal requested 6mo penalty cap and SOC2 attestation in contract.

Blockers: procurement needs a clear node-count to price reserved contract; security needs explicit HSM/KMS integration diagram for legal; data residency mapping for EU customers (Peregrine has EU customers served from NA; needs region routing).

POC plan (agreed): 1) 48h sustained throughput test at 60% load on 4x reserved nodes vs 8x baseline; 2) quantization fidelity sweep on 10 eval prompts (finance domain); 3) 24h KV cache effectiveness run measuring token-cost reduction. Deliverables: perf report, recommended reserved capacity, and a draft SLA appendix.
